skill.name: resolving-merge-conflicts
skill.description: Guides careful resolution of active Git merge or rebase conflicts by preserving intent and running checks.
skill.summary: Resolve Git conflicts through source review, hunk decisions, checks, and final continuation.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around `--abort`, not executable shell syntax. The skill is prompt-only and contains no code, network calls, credential handling, or prompt injection text.

static_findings.snippet: 3. **Resolve each hunk.** Preserve both intents where possible. Where incompatible, pick the one mat

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 10 uses Markdown backticks to format the literal `--abort` Git option. There is no Ruby or shell execution context in SKILL.md.

content.value_statement: Merge and rebase conflicts interrupt delivery and can hide lost intent. This skill guides source review, hunk resolution, checks, and final Git continuation.
actual_capabilities: Guides inspection of the current merge or rebase state before editing conflicts.
Directs review of commit messages, pull requests, issues, and tickets to understand intent.
Supports hunk-by-hunk decisions that preserve both sides when possible.
Prompts users to run project checks, including typecheck, tests, and formatting.
Covers staging, committing, and continuing a rebase after conflicts are resolved.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or automated conflict editing.
Does not decide product intent without project history and user context.
Does not replace human review for complex or high-risk merges.
Assumes the repository has clear Git state and discoverable checks.

use_cases.title: Merge a Feature Branch
use_cases.description: Resolve conflicts between a feature branch and main while preserving both implementation intents.

use_cases.title: Rebase a Patch Series
use_cases.description: Work through repeated rebase conflicts with source review and final rebase continuation.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Release Branch
use_cases.description: Resolve late release conflicts, run project checks, and document trade-offs before committing.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect My Conflict
prompt_templates.prompt: I am in a Git merge conflict. Inspect the current state, list the conflicting files, and tell me what to read first.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me resolve the conflicts in [file]. Explain the intent on each side, then propose the safest hunk decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Run Checks After Merge
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the project checks for this repository. Run typecheck, tests, and format in the right order, then help fix merge-related failures.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Complex Rebase
prompt_templates.prompt: I am rebasing and conflicts keep appearing. For each conflict, trace the original intent, resolve it, stage changes, and continue the rebase.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for help with conflicts in a service file and its tests.
output: Reports the current merge state and names the conflicting files.
Summarizes intent from each side using history and related discussion.
Recommends hunk decisions, then asks to run tests and formatting.

output_examples.input: A maintainer is midway through a rebase with repeated conflicts.
output: Identifies the next conflict and the commits that introduced each side.
Suggests preserving compatible behavior and documenting any trade-off.
Stages the resolved files and continues the rebase after checks pass.

output_examples.input: A release engineer sees conflicts just before a branch cut.
output: Focuses on the release goal before choosing between incompatible changes.
Runs the repository checks after resolution.
Highlights any risky trade-off for final review before commit.

best_practices: Read history and linked project context before changing conflict hunks.
Preserve both change intents when they are compatible.
Run checks after resolution and fix failures caused by the merge.
anti_patterns: Choosing one side of a conflict without understanding why both changes exist.
Adding new behavior while resolving a conflict.
Skipping tests, typecheck, or formatting after editing conflict files.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps resolve active Git merge or rebase conflicts with source review, checks, and final continuation.

faq.question: Does it edit files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow for the AI assistant to inspect, reason, edit, and verify within your repository.

faq.question: Can it help during a rebase?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes staging resolved files and continuing the rebase until all commits are processed.

faq.question: How does it choose between conflicting changes?
faq.answer: It favors preserving both intents, then follows the stated merge goal when changes cannot coexist.

faq.question: What checks should I run?
faq.answer: It tells the assistant to discover project checks, usually typecheck, tests, and formatting.

faq.question: Is this a security-sensitive skill?
faq.answer: It is prompt-only and contains no executable code, but it mentions a Git option in Markdown.
